basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 30.' and it opens 'Vers. 30. Ascenditque Lot de Segor. Quaerendum est quare, cum ipse petierit ut Segor'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 30. Ascenditque Lot de Segor. Quaerendum est quare, cum ipse petierit ut Segor habitaret, hortante angelo ut in monte salvaretur, iterum relicta Segor montem conscenderit. Sed ex hoc vera videtur Hebraeorum opinio qui dicunt hanc civitatem tertio terrae motu corruisse. Hoc sciens Lot timuit ibi esse, reputans apud se quia si aliis stantibus haec ceciderat | multo facilius nunc aliis pereuntibus ipsa quoque posset perire. Et propter hoc peccatum infidelitatis, quia angelo non credidit, dicunt contigisse ei scelus incesti.
